config.title: Media queries

intro.title: Media queries
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a responsive web page that adapts its layout and styling based on the screen size of the device. You will learn the core concept of media queries, which are CSS rules that apply different styles under specific conditions, such as screen width. The main technology involved is CSS, using the @media rule to create breakpoints for mobile, tablet, and desktop views. By the end, you'll understand how to make your designs flexible and user-friendly across various devices.
intro.usecase: Media queries are essential for creating responsive websites that adapt to different screen sizes, from desktops to smartphones. In real-world software, you'll use them to adjust layouts in dashboards, ensuring data tables and charts rearrange for mobile viewing. They also control form layouts, making input fields stack vertically on smaller screens, and modify navigation menus to switch from horizontal bars to hamburger menus on tablets and phones.

objectives: Implement a basic media query to conditionally apply CSS rules
Configure breakpoints for different screen sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop)
Apply responsive typography by adjusting font sizes with media queries
Construct a responsive layout that changes structure at specific breakpoints
Manipulate element visibility and positioning across viewport sizes
Integrate multiple media queries to create a cohesive responsive design
Update existing CSS to make a static layout responsive

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure to style
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML file with a container and several content boxes that we'll style with CSS media queries. Start by adding a <div> with class 'container' that contains three <div> elements with class 'box'.
steps.hint: You'll need to write the basic HTML structure first. Remember to use proper HTML syntax with opening and closing tags.

steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>Media Query Practice</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Add your container and boxes here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic HTML structure ready for styling with CSS media queries.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a container div with three box divs inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a container div with exactly three box divs inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a container div with class 'container' and inside it, add three divs with class 'box'.

steps.title: Add base CSS styles for desktop view
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file named 'styles.css' and add base styles for a container and boxes that work well on desktop screens. Start by styling the container to be a flex container with centered content.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS file in the same directory as your HTML file. Use flexbox to arrange items horizontally with space between them.
steps.seedCode:
/* Add your base CSS styles for desktop view here */
/* Style the container as a flex container with centered content */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file with base styles that establish a desktop-friendly layout using flexbox for the container.
successCriteria: The CSS file exists and contains styles for a .container class with flex display properties appropriate for desktop layout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the CSS file, but the container styles might be incomplete. Make sure to use flex display properties and appropriate spacing for desktop layout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS file doesn't contain the required styles. Create a CSS file named 'styles.css' and add base styles for a container using flexbox for desktop layout.

steps.title: Understand the @media rule syntax
steps.instruction: Add a CSS comment that explains the basic structure of a media query using the @media rule syntax.
steps.hint: Write a comment that describes the pattern: @media media-type and (media-feature) { /* CSS rules */ }
steps.expectedOutcome: A comment is added that explains the basic structure of media queries.
successCriteria: A CSS comment is present that describes the @media rule syntax pattern.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a comment, but it doesn't fully explain the @media rule syntax. Make sure your comment shows the pattern: @media media-type and (media-feature) { /* CSS rules */ }
steps.feedbackWrong: No comment explaining the @media rule syntax was found. Add a CSS comment that describes the basic structure: @media media-type and (media-feature) { /* CSS rules */ }

steps.title: Create your first media query for tablets
steps.instruction: Add a media query that targets screens with a maximum width of 768px. Inside the media query, adjust the container width to 90% and reduce the box margins to 10px.
steps.hint: Use @media (max-width: 768px) { ... } to target tablet-sized screens. Inside the curly braces, write CSS rules that will apply only when the screen width is 768px or less.
steps.expectedOutcome: A media query is added that targets screens up to 768px wide, with container width set to 90% and box margins reduced to 10px.
successCriteria: The code contains @media (max-width: 768px) with rules setting container width to 90% and margins to 10px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your media query syntax is correct and includes both the width adjustment and margin changes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query for tablets isn't quite right. Make sure you're using @media (max-width: 768px) and adjusting both the container width and margins inside it.

steps.title: Add a mobile-specific media query
steps.instruction: Add a media query for mobile screens with max-width: 480px that changes the layout to a single column and reduces font sizes.
steps.hint: Use @media (max-width: 480px) to target small screens, then add CSS rules inside to modify the container and text.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new media query for max-width: 480px is added, containing rules to change layout to column and adjust font sizes.
successCriteria: The media query targets max-width: 480px and includes at least one rule for layout (e.g., flex-direction: column) and one for font size.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a media query, but it might be missing either the layout change or font size adjustment. Check if both are included.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mobile media query is not present or doesn't target max-width: 480px. Review the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Use min-width media queries
steps.instruction: Add a media query using min-width: 769px to demonstrate building up from mobile styles. Place it after your existing media queries.
steps.hint: Use @media (min-width: 769px) { /* styles for desktop */ } to apply styles when the viewport is at least 769px wide.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new media query with min-width: 769px is added to the CSS file, showing how to progressively enhance styles for larger screens.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a valid @media (min-width: 769px) rule placed after the existing media queries.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your media query uses the correct syntax: @media (min-width: 769px) { /* styles */ }.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query is missing or has incorrect syntax. Review the @media rule and min-width property.

steps.title: Combine multiple conditions in media queries
steps.instruction: Create a media query that targets screens between 481px and 768px (inclusive) by using both min-width and max-width conditions together.
steps.hint: Use the @media rule with both conditions separated by 'and'. For example: @media (min-width: 481px) and (max-width: 768px) { ... }
steps.expectedOutcome: A new media query that applies styles only when the screen width is between 481px and 768px.
successCriteria: The media query uses both min-width: 481px and max-width: 768px conditions connected with 'and'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your media query includes both min-width and max-width conditions connected with 'and'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to create a media query that uses both min-width and max-width to target screens between 481px and 768px.

steps.title: Add orientation-based media queries
steps.instruction: Add a media query that uses (orientation: portrait) to adjust the container's flex-direction to column.
steps.hint: Use @media (orientation: portrait) { ... } to target portrait orientation devices.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS will include a media query that changes the container's flex-direction to column when the device is in portrait orientation.
successCriteria: A media query with (orientation: portrait) is added and sets flex-direction: column on the container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your media query uses (orientation: portrait) and sets flex-direction: column.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query for portrait orientation is missing or incorrect. Check the syntax and property.

steps.title: Test media queries with browser tools
steps.instruction: Open your browser's developer tools and activate the responsive design mode to test all your media queries at different screen sizes.
steps.hint: In most browsers, press F12 or right-click and select 'Inspect' to open developer tools. Look for a mobile/tablet icon or 'Toggle device toolbar' to enter responsive design mode.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should be able to see your styles adapt as you resize the viewport in responsive design mode, confirming all media queries work correctly.
successCriteria: Media queries are tested at multiple screen sizes
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've opened developer tools, but make sure to activate responsive design mode and test at least three different screen sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop).
steps.feedbackWrong: The testing step wasn't completed. Please open browser developer tools, activate responsive design mode, and test your media queries at different screen sizes.

steps.title: Review and refine breakpoints
steps.instruction: Add a comment above each media query explaining its purpose and target device.
steps.hint: Write a brief comment like /* Tablet styles */ or /* Mobile styles */ above each @media rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each media query will have a descriptive comment explaining its breakpoint purpose.
successCriteria: All media queries have explanatory comments above them describing their target devices or conditions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some comments, but make sure every media query has an explanatory comment above it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media queries don't have explanatory comments. Add comments above each @media rule to explain what device or condition it targets.
